steps.title: Decide what one output row represents
steps.change: Each row is a supplier with its original spelling and contact fields. The sample contains three suppliers. Suppliers is the only source because country, email and supplier identity are all on one supplier record; each supplier can be checked independently.
steps.added_sql: SELECT SupplierID, CompanyName, Country, Email FROM Suppliers ORDER BY SupplierID;
steps.sql: SELECT SupplierID, CompanyName, Country, Email FROM Suppliers ORDER BY SupplierID;

steps.title: Keep suppliers with any issue
steps.change: Supplier 1 passes both checks and leaves the issue report. Suppliers 2 and 3 remain.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT SupplierID, CompanyName, Country, Email FROM Suppliers
WHERE Country IS NULL
   OR TRIM(LOWER(Country)) != 'india'
   OR TRIM(Email) IS NULL
   OR LENGTH(TRIM(Email)) = 0;

steps.title: Build the issue text
steps.change: The CASE expression labels supplier 2 with both issues and supplier 3 with a missing country. The combined condition is checked first.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT SupplierID, CompanyName, Country, Email,
    CASE
        WHEN Country IS NULL
             AND (TRIM(Email) IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(Email)) = 0)
            THEN 'Country missing; No email'
        WHEN TRIM(LOWER(Country)) != 'india'
             AND (TRIM(Email) IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(Email)) = 0)
            THEN 'Outside India; No email'
        WHEN Country IS NULL THEN 'Country missing'
        WHEN TRIM(LOWER(Country)) != 'india' THEN 'Outside India'
        WHEN TRIM(Email) IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(Email)) = 0 THEN 'No email'
    END AS issue
FROM Suppliers
